Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". - loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). It validates the caching structure during development. */} 17 18 With [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) enabled, `use cache` and `` let you control what gets cached and what streams in dynamically. When these are in the right place, client-side navigations are instant. 19 20 The [`unstable_instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) route segment config helps you place `` boundaries and `use cache` correctly. Add it to any page or layout and Next.js will check during development that navigating to that route produces an instant [static shell](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell). 21 22 This guide starts with a product page that loads instantly on navigation, then shows how to catch and fix a page where a misplaced `` boundary blocks the navigation. Nothing visible changes until the server finishes rendering. 23 24 > **Good to know:** A navigation is considered **instant** when, assuming caches are warm, the page renders without waiting on any network request. Cached content appears immediately and anything uncached streams in behind a `` fallback. A navigation is considered **blocking** when uncached data outside a `` boundary forces the old page to stay visible until the server finishes rendering. 25 26 ## A page that navigates instantly 27 28 A product page at `/store/[slug]` that fetches two pieces of data: product details (name, price) and live inventory. 29 30 - There is no `generateStaticParams`, meaning `slug` is only known at request time 31 - Both components await `params` to get the `slug`, which suspends. Each has its own `` boundary 32 - **Product info** rarely changes and is queried from the db using a cached function 33 - **Inventory** must be fresh on each request. The db query is inside a `` boundary 34 35 ```tsx filename="app/store/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={4,9-14,32-34} 36 import { Suspense } from 'react' 37 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 38 39 export const unstable_instant = true 40 41 export default function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/store/[slug]'>) { 42 return ( 43

}> 48 49 50
51 ) 52 } 53 54 type Params = PageProps<'/store/[slug]'>['params'] 55 56 async function ProductInfo({ params }: { params: Params }) { 57 const { slug } = await params 58 const product = await getProduct(slug) 59 return ( 60 <> 61

{product.name}

${product.price}

{item.count} in stock

76 } 77 ``` 78 79 The [`unstable_instant`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) export tells Next.js to check that navigating to this page from any other page in your app is instant. It does this during development. If a component would delay the transition (for example, by fetching uncached data without a local `` boundary), the error overlay tells you which one and suggests a fix. 80 81 Validation runs automatically on every page load using the real request from your browser, so dynamic params like `[slug]` are checked against actual values as you navigate. 82 83 ## Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools 84 85 The Next.js DevTools let you see what users see on page loads and client navigations before dynamic data streams in. Use it to verify your loading states look right, check that the right content appears immediately, and iterate on where to place `` boundaries. 86 87 The Navigation Inspector is available when Cache Components is enabled: 88 89 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4} 90 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 91 92 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 93 cacheComponents: true, 94 } 95 96 export default nextConfig 97 ``` 98 99 Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Navigation Inspector**, then click **Start Capturing**. While capturing is active: 100 101 - Refresh the page to freeze the initial static UI generated for the route, before any dynamic data streams in. 102 - Click a link to freeze the prefetched UI for the destination route. 103 104 When the UI is frozen, click **Continue Rendering** to let the current navigation finish while keeping the Navigation Inspector in capturing mode. Click **Stop Capturing** when you are done inspecting loading states. 105 106 Try refreshing the product page. Two separate fallbacks appear: "Loading product..." and "Checking availability...". On the first visit the cache is cold and both fallbacks are visible. Navigate to the page again and the product name appears immediately from cache. 107 108 Now click a link from `/store/shoes` to `/store/hats`. The product name and price appear immediately (cached). "Checking availability..." shows where inventory will stream in. 109 110 > **Good to know:** Page loads and client navigations can produce different shells. Client-side hooks like `useSearchParams` suspend on page loads (search params are not known at build time) but resolve synchronously on client navigations (the router already has the params). 111 112
113 Why page loads and client navigations produce different shells 114 115 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root, including all layouts. Anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the entire document tree. 116 117 On a client navigation (clicking `next/link`), Next.js only re-renders below the layout that the source and destination routes share. Components above that shared layout are not re-rendered. This means that a `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but for a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, the shared layout is `/store` and Next.js renders the part of the document below that point. The root `` sits above it and does not trigger for this navigation. 118 119 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can appear in the instant shell on a client navigation but behind a fallback on a page load. 120 121
122 123 ## Prevent regressions with e2e tests 124 125 Validation catches structural problems during development. To prevent regressions as the codebase evolves, the `@next/playwright` package includes an `instant()` helper that asserts on exactly what appears in the instant shell: 126 127 ```typescript filename="e2e/navigation.test.ts" 128 import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test' 129 import { instant } from '@next/playwright' 130 131 test('product title appears instantly', async ({ page }) => { 132 await page.goto('/store/shoes') 133 134 await instant(page, async () => { 135 await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]') 136 await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap') 137 }) 138 139 // After instant() exits, dynamic content streams in 140 await expect(page.locator('text=in stock')).toBeVisible() 141 }) 142 ``` 143 144 Inside the `instant()` callback, only the static shell is visible. After the callback finishes, dynamic content streams in and you can assert on the full page. 145 146 There is no need to write an `instant()` test for every navigation. Use `instant()` for the user flows that matter most. In the future build-time `instant` validation will be available to cover a broader set of navigation cases. 147 148 ## Fixing a navigation that blocks 149 150 Now consider a different route, `/shop/[slug]`. For the sake of this example it has the same data requirements as `/store/[slug]`, but is implemented without local `` boundaries or caching: 151 152 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" 153 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 154 155 export default async function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) { 156 const { slug } = await props.params 157 const product = await db.products.findBySlug(slug) 158 const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) 159 return ( 160

}>{children} 181 182 183 ) 184 } 185 ``` 186 187 On an initial page load, the root `` catches the async work and streams the page in behind the `fallback`. 188 189 Everything appears to work. But on a client navigation from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`, the shared layout is `/shop` and only the content below it re-renders. The root `` boundary is above that layout and is not triggered for this navigation. The page fetches uncached data with no local boundary, blocking the navigation until the server finishes rendering. 190 191 You can see this with the DevTools. Try a **page load**: the root `` catches everything and "Loading..." appears. Now try a **client navigation** between two `/shop/` pages: no prefetched UI shows up because there is no `` boundary below the shared layout. Navigations from other routes to `/shop/` appear blocked too. 192 193 ### Step 1: Add instant validation 194 195 Add an `unstable_instant` export to the page to surface the problem: 196 197 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={3} 198 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 199 200 export const unstable_instant = true 201 202 export default async function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) { 203 const { slug } = await props.params 204 const product = await db.products.findBySlug(slug) 205 const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) 206 return ( 207
208

{product.name}

${product.price}

210

{item.count} in stock

211
212 ) 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 Next.js now simulates navigations at every shared layout boundary in the route. In this case, both components await `params` and access uncached data. These need to be wrapped by a `` boundary. The first thing validation catches is the `await params` at the top level. 217 218 ### Step 2: Fix the validation error 219 220 There is no `generateStaticParams` here, `slug` is only known at request time. Because awaiting `params` suspends, the page component can't do it at the top level. Instead, move the `await params` into separate components, pass `params` to each, and wrap them with ``. 221 222 For each component, decide: 223 224 **Product details** (name, price) rarely change. Cache the data function with `use cache`: 225 226 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" 227 async function ProductInfo({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { 228 const { slug } = await params 229 const product = await getProduct(slug) 230 return ( 231 <> 232

{product.name}

Consider using [`"use cache: remote"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for persistent caching. 245 246 **Inventory** must be fresh each request. Leave it uncached: 247 248 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" 249 async function Inventory({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { 250 const { slug } = await params 251 const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) 252 return

{item.count} in stock

253 } 254 ``` 255 256 The page passes `params` to each component and wraps them with ``: 257 258 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={4,9-14} 259 import { Suspense } from 'react' 260 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 261 262 export const unstable_instant = true 263 264 export default function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) { 265 return ( 266
267 Loading product...

}> 268 269 270 Checking availability...

274 ) 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 Validation passes. Open the DevTools and try a client navigation. The product name and price appear immediately, and "Checking availability..." shows where inventory will stream in. 279 280
281 How validation simulates different navigations 282 283 When you add `unstable_instant` to a route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. 284 285 For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: 286 287 - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. 288 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 289 290 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 291 292
293 294 ## Opting out with `instant = false` 295 296 Not every layout or page can be instant. A dashboard layout that reads cookies and fetches user-specific data might be too dynamic for the first visit. You can set `instant = false` on any layout or page to exempt it from validation: 297 298 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 299 export const unstable_instant = false 300 ``` 301 302 This tells validation: navigating to `/dashboard` from outside does not need to be instant, but sibling navigations within it still do. Navigating from `/dashboard/a` to `/dashboard/b` can still be checked by adding `instant` to the page segments under `/dashboard`. 303 304 ## Next steps 305 306 - [`instant` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) for all configuration options, including runtime prefetching and incremental adoption with `instant = false` 307 - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering 308 - [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) for how to expire cached data with `cacheLife` and `updateTag` 309

To prevent regressions as the codebase evolves, the `@next/playwright` package includes an `instant()` helper that asserts on exactly what appears in the instant shell: ```typescript filename="e2e/navigation.test.ts" import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test' import { instant } from '@next/playwright' test('product title appears instantly', async ({ page }) => { await page.goto('/store/shoes') await instant(page, async () => { await page.click('a[href="/store/hats"]') await expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Baseball Cap') }) // After instant() exits, dynamic content streams in await expect(page.locator('text=in stock')).toBeVisible() }) ``` Inside the `instant()` callback, only the static shell is visible. After the callback finishes, dynamic content streams in and you can assert on the full page. There is no need to write an `instant()` test for every navigation. Use `instant()` for the user flows that matter most. In the future build-time `instant` validation will be available to cover a broader set of navigation cases. ## Fixing a navigation that blocks Now consider a different route, `/shop/[slug]`. For the sake of this example it has the same data requirements as `/store/[slug]`, but is implemented without local `` boundaries or caching: ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" import { db } from '@/lib/db' export default async function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) { const { slug } = await props.params const product = await db.products.findBySlug(slug) const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) return (

{product.name}

${product.price}

{item.count} in stock

) } ``` The root layout wraps `{children}` in a `` boundary: ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={9} export default function RootLayout({ children, }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return ( Loading...

}>{children} ) } ``` On an initial page load, the root `` catches the async work and streams the page in behind the `fallback`. Everything appears to work. But on a client navigation from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`, the shared layout is `/shop` and only the content below it re-renders. The root `` boundary is above that layout and is not triggered for this navigation. The page fetches uncached data with no local boundary, blocking the navigation until the server finishes rendering. You can see this with the DevTools. Try a **page load**: the root `` catches everything and "Loading..." appears. Now try a **client navigation** between two `/shop/` pages: no prefetched UI shows up because there is no `` boundary below the shared layout. Navigations from other routes to `/shop/` appear blocked too. ### Step 1: Add instant validation Add an `unstable_instant` export to the page to surface the problem: ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={3} import { db } from '@/lib/db' export const unstable_instant = true export default async function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) { const { slug } = await props.params const product = await db.products.findBySlug(slug) const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) return (

{product.name}

${product.price}

{item.count} in stock

) } ``` Next.js now simulates navigations at every shared layout boundary in the route. In this case, both components await `params` and access uncached data. These need to be wrapped by a `` boundary. The first thing validation catches is the `await params` at the top level. ### Step 2: Fix the validation error There is no `generateStaticParams` here, `slug` is only known at request time. Because awaiting `params` suspends, the page component can't do it at the top level. Instead, move the `await params` into separate components, pass `params` to each, and wrap them with ``. For each component, decide: **Product details** (name, price) rarely change. Cache the data function with `use cache`: ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" async function ProductInfo({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { const { slug } = await params const product = await getProduct(slug) return ( <>

{product.name}

${product.price}

) } async function getProduct(slug: string) { 'use cache' return db.products.findBySlug(slug) } ``` > **Good to know:** In serverless deployments, in-memory caching with `"use cache"` will not persist across instances. Consider using [`"use cache: remote"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for persistent caching. **Inventory** must be fresh each request. Leave it uncached: ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" async function Inventory({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { const { slug } = await params const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) return

{item.count} in stock

} ``` The page passes `params` to each component and wraps them with ``: ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={4,9-14} import { Suspense } from 'react' import { db } from '@/lib/db' export const unstable_instant = true export default function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) { return (
Loading product...

}> Checking availability...

}>
) } ``` Validation passes. Open the DevTools and try a client navigation. The product name and price appear immediately, and "Checking availability..." shows where inventory will stream in.
How validation simulates different navigations When you add `unstable_instant` to a route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows.
## Opting out with `instant = false` Not every layout or page can be instant. A dashboard layout that reads cookies and fetches user-specific data might be too dynamic for the first visit. You can set `instant = false` on any layout or page to exempt it from validation: ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" export const unstable_instant = false ``` This tells validation: navigating to `/dashboard` from outside does not need to be instant, but sibling navigations within it still do. Navigating from `/dashboard/a` to `/dashboard/b` can still be checked by adding `instant` to the page segments under `/dashboard`. ## Next steps - [`instant` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) for all configuration options, including runtime prefetching and incremental adoption with `instant = false` - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering - [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) for how to expire cached data with `cacheLife` and `updateTag`

Fixed — the product title now appears immediately on navigation. **The problem:** `app/product/page.tsx` awaited `getInventory()` at the top level of the page component. That function calls `connection()`, marking the data as uncached and request-time-only. With Cache Components enabled (this project's `next.config.ts`), uncached data outside a `` boundary makes the navigation *blocking*: clicking "View Product" from home kept the old page visible until the server finished rendering, so even the static title waited on the inventory fetch. This is exactly the anti-pattern described in this version's `instant-navigation` guide. **The fix** in `app/product/page.tsx`: - The page component is now synchronous, so the `

Premium Widget

` is part of the prerendered static shell that renders instantly from the prefetch. - The inventory fetch moved into an async `` component wrapped in ``, so the stock count and price stream in behind a "Checking availability..." fallback. - Added `export const unstable_instant = true`, which makes Next.js validate during development that navigating to this page stays instant — if someone later adds blocking data outside a boundary, the dev overlay will flag it. Verified with a production build: `/product` now shows as `◐ (Partial Prerender)`, and the prerendered HTML contains the title and the fallback. (The build also auto-adjusted `tsconfig.json` — standard Next.js housekeeping.) One judgment call: I left the price inside the dynamic section because `getInventory()` currently generates it per-request alongside the stock count. If price is actually stable, it could be cached with `use cache` and moved into the instant shell too.
